recognize_zh: 這是光穿透式血小板凝集檢查（LTA）的曲線與數據：只有高劑量 ristocetin（1.2 mg/mL）出現完整凝集（最大 104%），ADP、epinephrine、arachidonic acid 幾乎平坦、collagen 僅微弱反應；「只對 ristocetin 有反應、其他促效劑都不凝集」是 Glanzmann 血小板無力症的典型模式。
features: Channel 1, ristocetin 1.2 mg/mL: rapid, full aggregation curve with maximal amplitude 104%
Channel 2, low-dose ristocetin 0.6 mg/mL: no aggregation (1%), excluding type 2B VWD/platelet-type VWD hyper-responsiveness
Arachidonic acid 0%, epinephrine 1%, ADP 10%: essentially flat tracings with only shape-change deflection
Collagen: slow, reduced response reaching about 30% maximal aggregation
Pattern of absent aggregation to multiple agonists with preserved ristocetin agglutination
describe_en: This figure shows light transmission platelet aggregometry tracings with the corresponding summary table. High-dose ristocetin (1.2 mg/mL) produces complete agglutination with a maximal amplitude of 104%, whereas low-dose ristocetin (0.6 mg/mL) shows no response. Arachidonic acid, epinephrine, and ADP produce essentially no aggregation (0 to 10%), and collagen gives only a slow, markedly reduced response (about 30%). Absent aggregation to physiologic agonists with preserved ristocetin-induced agglutination indicates a defect of the fibrinogen receptor, and in conjunction with a normal platelet count, normal VWF studies, and prolonged PFA closure times, the findings are consistent with Glanzmann thrombasthenia (integrin αIIbβ3 deficiency).

ddx.vs: Shows the opposite pattern: absent ristocetin agglutination with normal responses to ADP, collagen, epinephrine, and arachidonic acid, plus giant platelets and thrombocytopenia.
Reduced ristocetin response with normal aggregation to other agonists and abnormal VWF antigen/activity, whereas VWF levels here are normal to high.

ddx.dx: Aspirin/NSAID effect or storage pool/secretion defect
ddx.vs: Abolishes arachidonic acid response and the secondary wave to ADP/epinephrine but preserves primary wave aggregation to high-dose ADP, unlike the flat tracings here.
Also impairs aggregation, but plasma fibrinogen and coagulation times (PT/APTT) are markedly abnormal, whereas they are normal in this patient.
